entries.summary: The three-session Nasdaq/QQQ outlook remains Bearish for October 30, November 2 and November 3. Reuters observed Nasdaq-100 futures -2.41% at 07:14 ET, compared with -2.16% at 04:04 ET in the prior assessment, reinforcing the already bearish earnings-led setup rather than creating a new regime. NasDecode's 07:43 ET dashboard score is -28/100 (prior -29), 10Y/2Y yields are 4.910%/4.569% (curve +34.1 bp), and Brent/WTI are $117.55/$104.02. Thursday's QQQ/SOX/breadth/VXN remain previous-session observations, not Friday cash-market confirmation. Thursday's 56/98 advancing Nasdaq-100 constituents still suggest weakness was concentrated in major technology weights rather than full capitulation. MediaTek, SK hynix and Tokyo Electron demand signals support the longer-term AI equipment/memory pipeline without proving a Friday rebound.

The latest NasDecode model remains -28/100; Thursday's mega-cap basket fell -2.09% against QQQ -1.42%, and VXN was elevated at 25.18 at the previous close. editorial.marketOverview: Nasdaq begins the final October trading session under the same bearish three-day regime. Reuters observed Nasdaq-100 futures down 2.41% at 07:14 ET as Amazon's higher AI infrastructure spending and Intel's cash-burn warning pressured major technology names. The prior U.S. regular session saw Nasdaq down about 1.38%, QQQ 1.42% and SOX 1.42%, while the mega-cap basket lagged QQQ. This is a coherent technology leadership shock, but it remains important to distinguish Friday futures from the U.S. cash market, which has not opened at this checkpoint. NasDecode's latest 07:43 ET model score of -28/100 remains negative, while previous-close breadth still shows mixed participation.
editorial.whatChanged: The official Q3 Employment Cost Index has now been released at 08:30 ET: civilian compensation increased 0.8% quarter-on-quarter versus 0.9% in Q2, and civilian wages increased 0.7%. A secondary pre-release calendar listed 0.8% consensus, so this appears in line rather than a fresh inflation shock; no time-aligned post-release market response is verified. Reuters' 07:14 ET Nasdaq-100 futures reading of -2.41% is weaker than the prior assessment's 04:04 ET -2.16%, though both belong to the same premarket earnings selloff. The NasDecode score improved marginally from -29 to -28 and yields eased slightly. Curated Open Watch expanded from 86 to 87 with a Binance breach record describing $6.3 billion in impact, an escalation in incident scale but not confirmed as a separate Nasdaq driver.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The central conflict is between strong demand for AI computation and the cash flows needed to finance it. Amazon's and Intel's results have shifted the focus from revenue growth to capital intensity, debt funding and margins; Friday's weakness in Nvidia and AMD premarket indicates that the repricing is not isolated to the companies that reported. Lower 10Y and 2Y yields offer valuation relief, but may also represent a defensive bid, and they were recorded before the ECI release. The 0.8% compensation reading removes one possible upside labor-cost surprise but does not erase elevated oil or the Fed's hawkish settlement-derived probabilities. Semiconductor relative strength, volatility and breadth still require a Friday cash-market test.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday October 30 remains the pivotal session. The verified 08:30 ET labor-cost report is not, by itself, evidence that the earnings-led selloff has reversed. The baseline is a downside-biased, volatile U.S. opening, followed by a decision point: either technology shares absorb the shock and begin to stabilize or selling spreads from mega-cap leaders to more of the Nasdaq-100 and chip universe. Monday November 2 may bring a consolidation attempt if Friday's breadth and volatility improve, while Apple and ON Semiconductor earnings are listed as event risks. Tuesday November 3 adds listed AMD, Astera Labs and Skyworks reports, which could test whether memory and accelerator demand can offset AI-financing fears. These are conditional paths, not observed future returns.
editorial.bullCase: A constructive recovery would rest on slowing wage-cost momentum, lower Treasury yields and evidence that AI infrastructure demand is still expanding. The BLS ECI shows 0.8% quarterly compensation growth after 0.9%, while NasDecode's 07:43 ET Treasury yields were 4.910%/4.569%, down materially versus the prior close. Previous-session Nasdaq-100 breadth was still positive at 56 of 98 covered names, and positive memory/equipment demand signals from Asian suppliers argue against a sudden end-demand collapse. A credible upgrade needs synchronized Friday confirmation: QQQ reclaiming its opening gap and Thursday close, SOX outperforming, representative chip breadth above 50%, Nasdaq-100 breadth above 60% and VXN below 24. None of those cash-session conditions is yet verified.
editorial.bearCase: The downside scenario is an earnings-led technology de-rating that broadens into forced risk reduction. Reuters' 07:14 ET Nasdaq-100 futures decline of 2.41%, Amazon down 6.3% and Intel down more than 25% premarket, together with Nvidia and AMD weakness, support this concern. Thursday's VXN close of 25.18 and Brent above $117 add volatility and inflation constraints, while Asian chip losses show global spillover. The Binance incident may contribute to speculative-market stress, but no isolated transmission to Nasdaq has been established. Persistent Friday QQQ selling, SOX underperformance, representative chip breadth below one-third, Nasdaq-100 participation below 40% and VXN at or above 26 would strengthen this bear case.
editorial.watchNext: The immediate priority is to compare post-08:30 ET Treasury yields and Fed pricing with their pre-release baselines, without attributing a move to ECI unless the timing and broader news flow support it. At the 09:30 ET opening, capture time-aligned Nasdaq, QQQ, SOX/SOXX/SMH, Nasdaq-100 breadth, representative SOX constituent breadth, VXN/VIX and rates. Monitor Amazon, Intel, Nvidia, AMD and any genuinely new curated Open Watch events for broad-market confirmation.
